target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ (𝓢 : ArithmeticTheory) (K F : ArithmeticSentence → ArithmeticSentence),
    Def1 (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) K ∧ (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) ⪯ 𝓢 ∧
    Def2 𝓢 K ∧ Def3 𝓢 K ∧ Def4 𝓢 K ∧
    Def5 (𝗣𝗔 : ArithmeticTheory) F ∧
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡘 F φ)) ∧
    (∃ p, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K (∼p) 🡘 p)) ∧
    Entailment.Consistent 𝓢

translation: Target is the proposition that there exist an arithmetic theory 𝓢, a function K from arithmetic sentences to arithmetic sentences, and a function F of the same type, such that all of the following hold for those same choices. Here φ, ψ, and p range over closed arithmetic sentences, and →, ↔, and ¬ inside a sentence denote object-language connectives. (1) For every φ, if PA proves φ, then PA proves K(φ). (2) Every sentence PA proves is also proved by 𝓢. (3) For every φ and then every ψ, 𝓢 proves K(φ → ψ) → (K(φ) → K(ψ)). (4) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(φ) → φ. (5) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) → φ). (6) There exists a ψ such that PA proves ψ ↔ ¬F(ψ). (7) For every φ, 𝓢 proves K(K(φ) ↔ F(φ)). (8) There exists a p such that 𝓢 proves K(K(¬p) ↔ p). (9) 𝓢 does not prove every arithmetic sentence. The witnesses ψ in (6) and p in (8) are quantified separately. In (7) and (8) the outer K applies to the entire biconditional. Condition (1) is a closure requirement on PA, not on 𝓢; (2) concerns inclusion of provable sentences, not literal inclusion of axiom sets. Neither K nor F is required to be given by an arithmetic formula.

divergences.description: The target requires `Def4 𝓢 K`: for every φ, 𝓢 proves K(Kφ → φ). This is exactly the known-factivity scheme the counterpart is supposed to omit, not the ordinary factivity it is supposed to retain (`Def3`). The addition rules out a consistent witness. For the asserted p, let E be (K(∼p) ↔ p) and T be (K(∼p) → ∼p). The p-clause gives K(E), and `Def4` gives K(T). Since E and T propositionally imply ∼p, PA necessitation, inclusion, and `Def2` yield K(∼p) in 𝓢. Factivity then gives both ∼p and E, while E and K(∼p) give p.

judgement.summary: Using arithmetic provability and an arbitrary sentence map F instead of Alexander’s epistemic structure and fixed W_m is the stated abstraction. Even as that abstract counterpart, the target fails: it asserts known factivity rather than leaving it out.
